newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan shipping talks begin.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan shipping talks begin.

text.p: Talks got underway Thursday between U.S. and Japanese officials to avert a $100,000-per-ship surcharge announced by the United States last week.
The surcharge, to apply to Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports, would become effective April 14 if no compromise is reached.
The U.S. Maritime Commission said last week it was imposing the charges in retaliation for unfair Japanese port practices.
In particular, the United States objects to the refusal of Japan to license non-Japanese companies to perform stevedoring or terminal operating services.
A U.S. Transportation Department official said the talks got underway late today and might either go into the night or continue Friday.

The proposed surcharge would be imposed each time a vessel owned or operated by Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK enters a U.S. port from abroad, but not from another U.S. port.
